text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Hi A, I'm helping you and your sisters talk through the house after your father's death. I'm sorry for your loss. Before any decisions, I'd like to hear what matters to you — could you share your thoughts on the house and the estate, in your own words? There's no rush and no judgment here; I just want to understand everyone's needs first.
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband, ideally at a family discount. But C hasn’t agreed, so we can’t move ahead unless she does. We haven’t settled the price or shares.

Hi B, I'm helping you and your sisters talk through the house after your father's death. I'm sorry for your loss. Before any decisions, I'd like to hear what matters to you — could you share your thoughts on the house and the estate, in your own words? There's no rush and no judgment here; I just want to understand everyone's needs first.

Thank you. I’d like us to find a fair way to deal with the house and the estate. I’m hoping my share could give me enough to start a dance studio, though I know we haven’t settled on the house’s value or anyone’s share yet.

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry for your loss. I've heard from A and B too. Before we talk solutions, I want to make sure I understand what matters to you. I heard you don't want to sign off on A buying at a "family discount," and you want B to be looked after. Could I restate that as: you want the house's value to be settled fairly and openly, so no one is shortchanged and everyone's interests are respected? Does that fit, or would you word it differently?
Yes, that’s close. I want a fair share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. B should be treated fairly too, but I can’t decide for her.

Thank you, A. Before we look at options, I want to make sure I understand what matters to you. I heard you'd like to buy the house with your husband, but you recognize C hasn't agreed and the price/shares aren't settled. Could I restate that as: you want a real chance to make the house your home, in a way your sisters can genuinely agree to? Does that fit, or would you word it differently?
Mostly. I want to buy it with my husband at a family discount, if C agrees.

Thank you, B. Before we look at options, I want to make sure I understand what matters to you. I heard you'd like a fair outcome and hope your share could help fund a dance studio. Could I restate that as: you want your share of the estate to be decided fairly, and enough financial support to pursue your goals? Does that fit, or would you word it differently?
Yes, that’s about right. I’d just say the studio is what I’m hoping to use my share for.

Thank you, A. When you say you want to buy at a family discount if C agrees — that's an outcome, and C has said she won't agree to a discount. So I want to check whether the underlying need fits this wording: you want a real chance to make the house your home, in a way your sisters can genuinely agree to. Does that capture what matters to you, or is there something else the discount would give you (for example, affordability, or feeling the house stays in the family)? There's no wrong answer — I just want to understand the need, not the specific price.
The discount would make it more manageable. Having a secure home and being financially independent matter to me.

Thank you, A — that's helpful. So the discount is about affordability, not the price itself. Let me check a wording that captures the need without naming the outcome: you want a genuinely affordable way to secure a home and stay financially independent, in a way your sisters can genuinely agree to. Does that fit? I won't record it until you say so.
Yes, that fits.

Thank you, C. All three concerns are now confirmed. Here are draft options that could meet all of them: (1) An independent appraisal so any price is transparent and fair to everyone. (2) A buys the house at the appraised fair value, possibly with a structured payment plan so it's manageable for her — without a discount below fair value. (3) Selling the house on the open market and dividing the estate fairly among all three. (4) Other combinations — e.g., A buys and B receives a larger share of other assets, or co-ownership. Does any of these move in the right direction? Even a small discomfort matters — a "no" just tells us what to add. What would you want included or changed?

An independent appraisal makes sense. I’m open to A buying at fair value, but I’m not agreeing to a payment plan or any arrangement that leaves me shortchanged. I’m not in a rush; we should work out the details openly.

Thank you, A. All three concerns are now confirmed. Here are draft options that could meet all of them: (1) An independent appraisal so any price is transparent and fair to everyone. (2) A buys the house at the appraised fair value, possibly with a structured payment plan so it's manageable for her — without a discount below fair value. (3) Selling the house on the open market and dividing the estate fairly among all three. (4) Other combinations — e.g., A buys and B receives a larger share of other assets, or co-ownership. Does any of these move in the right direction? Even a small discomfort matters — a "no" just tells us what to add. What would you want included or changed?
Option 2 is closest, but fair value may still be unaffordable. I’d want to explore payment terms that make it manageable, and we’d still need C’s agreement.

Thank you, B. All three concerns are now confirmed. Here are draft options that could meet all of them: (1) An independent appraisal so any price is transparent and fair to everyone. (2) A buys the house at the appraised fair value, possibly with a structured payment plan so it's manageable for her — without a discount below fair value. (3) Selling the house on the open market and dividing the estate fairly among all three. (4) Other combinations — e.g., A buys and B receives a larger share of other assets, or co-ownership. Does any of these move in the right direction? Even a small discomfort matters — a "no" just tells us what to add. What would you want included or changed?
An independent appraisal sounds fair, and A buying could work if the payment arrangement gives me access to my share in time to start the studio. I wouldn’t want to assume C agrees, though.

Thank you, C — helpful. I've noted this as a new concern: any payment arrangement must not leave you shortchanged. Does that wording fit? And to test a direction: an independent appraisal sets fair value; A buys at that value with a payment schedule, but your share is fully guaranteed (e.g., secured against the house or paid on an agreed schedule) so you're never shortchanged. Would that address your concern, or is there something it misses? Even a small discomfort is worth naming.
That wording fits. In principle, it could work, but I’d need clear terms proving my full fair share is protected—and B’s interests need to be addressed too. I’m not agreeing to a schedule yet.

Thank you, B — helpful. I've noted this as a new concern: you need access to your share in time to start the dance studio. Does that wording fit? And to test a direction: an independent appraisal sets fair value; A buys at that value with a payment schedule, but your share is paid on a timeline that works for the studio. Would that address your concern, or is there something it misses? Even a small discomfort is worth naming.
That could be a direction, yes, if the payment timing works for me—but I can’t say what timeline would be workable until I know the terms. And C would need to agree too.

Update from everyone: B says the direction could work if the payment timing works for her, but she needs to know the terms first — and she notes your agreement is essential too. Next step if you'd like it: we could agree in principle on (a) an independent appraisal, and (b) that any buyout terms must fully secure your share and fit B's timeline — with the specific terms to be drafted and reviewed by all three before anyone commits. Does that feel like a fair place to go next? Even small discomforts are worth naming.
Yes, that’s a fair next step. I’m agreeing to an appraisal and to reviewing proposed terms—not committing to a buyout. My share must be protected, and B needs to decide what works for her.
